merger_description:
Wollemi Capital Pty Ltd (**Wollemi Capital**) is a specialist climate investment firm that is proposing to establish a new investment trust (the WEG Australian Investment Trust) to facilitate further private capital investment in its renewables portfolio investment company, Wollemi Energy Group Holdings Pty Ltd.

Wollemi Energy Group Holdings Pty Ltd is the ultimate holding company for Wollemi Energy Group Pty Ltd.

Wollemi Energy Group Pty Ltd owns and operates MPower, a renewable energy generation and battery energy storage business.

As part of the establishment of the WEG Australian Investment Trust, it is proposed that:

* A new trustee entity, Wollemi Nominees 2 Pty Ltd, incorporated by Wollemi Capital, will be appointed as trustee of the WEG Australian Investment Trust.
* The WEG Australian Investment Trust will be managed by Wollemi Asset Management Pty Ltd, an entity established and managed by Wollemi Capital.
* The WEG Australian Investment Trust will receive capital investment from the Retail Employees Superannuation Trust (**REST**), for future investment in renewables and battery energy storage projects by Wollemi Energy Group Holdings Pty Ltd.

REST is an existing indirect investor in Wollemi Energy Group Holdings Pty Ltd via an existing investment trust established and managed by Wollemi Capital.

Wollemi Climate Investments Pty Ltd, an existing holder of issued voting shares in the capital of Wollemi Energy Group Holdings Pty Ltd, will also subscribe for new ordinary shares in Wollemi Energy Group Holdings Pty Ltd.

Before and after the proposed transaction, the relevant interests in Wollemi Energy Group Holdings Pty Ltd will be legally owned and managed by entities that are wholly-owned and controlled by Wollemi Capital.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. there is no horizontal consolidation or removal of a
competitor as a result of the Acquisition
b. REST is already an existing indirect investor in WEG
Holdings, and the Acquisition does not create any new
overlap in the supply of renewable energy generation and
battery storage assets
c. there does not appear to be any substantive change in the
control of WEG Holdings.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
